slides.texte_overlay:
small things that make you
seem incredibly well read

quoting one line

learn one great line from a book you loved and use it only when it truly fits. a single well placed quote does more than a dozen half remembered summaries.

knowing the author's story

learn a little about the life of the authors you read. knowing why a book was written makes every conversation about it far richer, deeper and more personal.

recommending the right book

keep a short mental list of books for different moods: comfort, adventure, ideas. people remember the friend who always knows exactly what they should read next.

a little context daily

spend 5 minutes a day learning the history behind famous books, paintings and ideas. context makes you sound well read even about things you haven't finished yet.

i spend 5 minutes a day on one lesson in the Sophia app about the history behind famous books and ideas. context makes you sound well read even about things you haven't finished.

slides.texte_overlay:
reading slowly

read fewer books, but read them properly, with a pencil in hand. people who truly understand five books always sound smarter than people who quickly skimmed fifty.
